line: Hi, I'm Ruth. I run the adult programs here: ESL, citizenship class, and a Thursday potluck that's mostly an excuse to meet people. Any of that useful?
Last month a retired judge and a woman from Guangzhou found out they'd lived on the same block in Queens. That's the whole point. Bring anything, even chips.
I'm trying to get the center on Grand to co-host something in the spring. Do you know Dr. Zhou over there?
choice1: You should just walk over and ask her.

line: Honest question. When we print flyers in Chinese, does anyone read them, or do they just make us feel good?
choice1: People read them. Put the date in big numbers.
choice2: Ask the people you want to come.

line: Thursday's potluck: I'd like you at the table with the three new families. You know how it feels to be new here. Will you come?
You seem to know people on both sides of Grand Avenue. Come to Thursday's potluck? I'd like you at the table with the new families.
Citizenship class attendance dropped by half this month. People won't write their address on a sign-up sheet anymore. I don't blame them.
choice1: Could they sign up without an address?
choice2: Maybe the class should meet somewhere else.

line: The federal grant came through. Two more ESL sections and paid interpreters. I've been asking for that budget line for six years.
choice2: Who decides who gets the spots?

line: I hear you've been at the center a lot. That's good. Tell them our doors are open too. Some days it feels like there's a wall down Grand Avenue.
choice2: People go where they feel comfortable.

line: Oh, hello. I won't keep you.
Sorry, I'm setting up for the six o'clock class. Grab me after?
